title: Polynomial sheaf differentials after evaluation are free on the generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $A\to B$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $\alpha:E\to B$ be a map of sheaves of sets. Let $P_E=A[E]$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto A(U)[E(U)]$ of polynomial algebras [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with evaluation $[e]\mapsto\alpha(e)$. Use sheaf differentials $\Omega_{P_E/A}$ obtained by sheafifying the sectionwise universal modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $B^{(E)}$ for the free module sheaf on $E$ of [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property], to distinguish it from a polynomial algebra. There is a canonical $B$-linear isomorphism
$$\Phi_E:B^{(E)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B,\qquad [e]\longmapsto\mathrm d[e]\otimes1.$$
For every map $v:E'\to E$ over $B$, the induced differential map $F(v):\Omega_{P_{E'}/A}\otimes_{P_{E'}}B\to\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B$ satisfies $F(v)\Phi_{E'}=\Phi_E B^{(v)}$, where $B^{(v)}$ sends $[e']$ to $[v(e')]$. No surjectivity assumption on evaluation is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08UJ (lemma-NL-represent-ext-class-ringed-topoi), proof, first paragraph: description of Omega as the sheaf associated to the sectionwise free B-modules. Naturality is for the indicated maps of polynomial generators.

proof.text: Put $Q(U)=A(U)[E(U)]$, $D(U)=\Omega_{Q(U)/A(U)}$, $T(U)=D(U)\otimes_{Q(U)}B(U)$ and $L(U)=\bigoplus_{e\in E(U)}B(U)[e]$, with coefficient and generator restriction maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] to $R=A(U)$, the arbitrary set $E(U)$ and the $Q(U)$-algebra $B(U)$ given by evaluation. It gives the $B(U)$-linear isomorphism $\phi_U:L(U)\to T(U)$ sending $[e]$ to $\mathrm dX_e\otimes1$. Its inverse sends $(\sum_e q_e\mathrm dX_e)\otimes b$ to $\sum_e\operatorname{ev}(q_e)b[e]$. The tensor symmetry needed to put the cited basis in this tensor order is $b\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b$, with inverse the same flip, well-defined by balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 00RX, lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, polynomial differential basis and its scalar extension; used in defos.tex Tag 08UJ, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: For an arrow $V\to U$, define $D(U)\to D(V)$ semilinearly over $Q(U)\to Q(V)$ by $\mathrm dq\mapsto\mathrm d(q|_V)$. This is the unique map supplied by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], since $q\mapsto\mathrm d(q|_V)$ is an $A(U)$-derivation. Uniqueness proves identity and composition. Evaluation commutes with restriction because $\alpha$ is a sheaf map; hence the restrictions of $T$ take $\mathrm dX_e\otimes b$ to $\mathrm dX_{e|_V}\otimes b|_V$. Thus both composites in the restriction square for $\phi_U$ take $b[e]$ to $\mathrm dX_{e|_V}\otimes b|_V$. They agree by the basis in step 1. Consequently $\phi:L\to T$ is an isomorphism of presheaves of $B$-modules, with inverse given objectwise by $\phi_U^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, sectionwise differential presheaf; universal derivations as in Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel] to the map of ring presheaves $A\to Q$. Since $A$ is already a sheaf and $Q^\#=P_E$, it identifies $D^\#$ with $\Omega_{P_E/A}$, carrying the image of $\mathrm dq$ to the differential of the image of $q$ in $P_E$. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] with ring presheaf $Q$ and module presheaves $D,B$, where $B$ has its evaluation action. Its sheafification is the original sheaf $B$, with the action of $Q^\#=P_E$ induced by evaluation. We obtain a canonical comparison $c:T^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B$, taking the sheafification image of $\mathrm dq\otimes b$ to $\mathrm d(\eta_Q(q))\otimes b$. This comparison is $B$-linear: multiplying $b$ by a local coefficient on either side gives the same displayed tensor, and the module sheafification universal property [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] extends this equality uniquely.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: Sheafify the inverse presheaf maps $\phi$ and $\phi^{-1}$ of step 2. Functoriality of module sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] shows that their sheafifications are inverse. By the construction in [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property], $L^\#=B^{(E)}$. Define $\Phi_E=c\phi^\#:B^{(E)}\to\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B$. Steps 1 and 3 give $\Phi_E([e])=\mathrm d[e]\otimes1$, and both factors are $B$-linear isomorphisms. The same free module universal property says a $B$-linear map out of $B^{(E)}$ is uniquely determined by these generator values, so this is the asserted canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08UJ, lemma-NL-represent-ext-class-ringed-topoi, first proof paragraph; free module construction in sites-modules.tex Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module.

proof.text: Let $v:E^{\prime}\to E$ be over $B$. On each object the polynomial map sends $X_{e^{\prime}}$ to $X_{v(e^{\prime})}$ and commutes with evaluation. The universal derivation property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore induces the differential map $\mathrm dq\mapsto\mathrm d(v(q))$; tensoring and module sheafification give the indicated $B$-linear $F(v)$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. In particular, $F(v)(\mathrm d[e^{\prime}]\otimes1)=\mathrm d[v(e^{\prime})]\otimes1$. The two maps $F(v)\Phi_{E^{\prime}}$ and $\Phi_E B^{(v)}$ thus have identical values on every generator $[e^{\prime}]$. They are equal by [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property]. All steps used arbitrary evaluation homomorphisms, never a surjection; the proof applies to empty and infinite variable sets as well.

source.place: Tag 08UJ, lemma-NL-represent-ext-class-ringed-topoi, first paragraph and the subsequent change of generators E-prime to E; generator calculation using sites-modules.tex Tag 04BL.

F : term f E' α' ⟶ term f E α, ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj.obj U) (p : (polynomialSheaf A E').obj.obj U), F.val.app U (tensorD f E' α' U b p) = tensorD f E α U b ((polynomialMap A v).hom.app U p)) ∧ (∀ F : term f E' α' ⟶ term f E α, (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj.obj U) (p : (polynomialSheaf A E').obj.obj U), F.val.app U (tensorD f E' α' U b p) = tensorD f E α U b ((polynomialMap A v).hom.app U p)) → (Φ E' α').hom ≫ F = (SheafFreeModule.free B).map v ≫ (Φ E α).hom))
